newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products close lower on soy drop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products close lower on soy drop.

text.p: A sharp drop in soybean futures pressed CBOT soy product futures to a lower close, traders said.
"There was a lot of talk about South American weather looking good," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Nearly ideal soybean crop conditions in South America and rapid seeding of the soy crop led the way down with fund selling cited in all pits, they said.
Soyoil also was hit by the posting of 1,425 lots of soyoil for delivery on the December contract. But heavy deliveries have been expected on the December which limited the impact.
Fund selling was noted in oil and commercials were on both sides of the market.
Cargill Inc bought 300 lots of January and sold 500 while ADM Investor Services bought 300 January, traders said.
Soymeal was lower but cash sources said end-users bought the break in soymeal.
"Meal tried to rally early but gave up. There was too much pressure from beans," Kucha said.
Soyoil closed 0.16 to 0.36 cent per lb lower, with December down 0.24 at 22.74. Soymeal was $1.00 to $2.80 per ton lower, with December down $1.60 at $237.90.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 24,000 contracts, above the 14,833 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 27,000 contracts, above the 26,059 traded Friday.
